items.title: Ruthie Foster interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 28, 2023
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] That little thing you just said reminded me of Nat Adderley... [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah. You know that’s the trick.

ctx.x: Basically hired me as a songwriter with, as a performer in development. In other words if they had chosen any of the songs I had written to record then that would lock me into basically not owning, first of all not owning those songs or the performance, or anything else. A lot of those contracts are really vague about owning the person, their name, their brand and I knew that. So I wrote songs, but I kept a few to myself too. And the songs that I did turn in, none of them really were contracted or basically…

That little thing you just said reminded me of Nat Adderley, who was contracted to write a tune and he wrote “The Work Song” and he said, “Wait a minute, I’m going to keep this for myself and I’ll write another one for you.”

Yeah. You know that’s the trick. That was recommended to me by my representation and really just asking around. I asked a lot of questions when I lived in New York. I was a very curious songwriter. And I think that’s how I ended up in certain circles and really learning a lot really quick while I was there. I was there for about three years and so I found myself in front of great songwriters like Julie Gold who wrote “From a Distance” and really picking their brains when it came to writing songs and the industry,…
